title: Shortcutlets: one-click composable admin remediations
creator: Rishi Patel
description:
Background: Oncall frequently performs multi-step remediations (eg. rotate a token, restart a service, clear a KV cache, requeue a job). Current runbooks are prose-heavy and require manual step execution across multiple consoles which increases mean time to remediation and exposes human error.

Goal: Build a small, low-risk framework of composable 'shortcutlets' — parameterized, idempotent admin actions that can be composed into a single one-click remediation flow from the Console or CLI. Shortcutlets are not full automation agents: they should require explicit operator intent (button/confirm or CLI flag), present a dry-run preview, emit structured audit events, and support safe rollback.

Non-goals: Replacing runbooks with autonomous repair agents, exposing privileged operations to self-serve non-operator users, or implementing broad automation scheduling in this work.

Proposed design:
- Define a shortcutlet manifest schema (JSON/YAML) that declares inputs, preconditions, dry-run steps, action steps, postchecks, rollback steps, required permissions, and telemetry hooks.
- Shortcutlets execute in a sandboxed runner service with a small, audited set of SDK helpers for common ops actions (restart-service, kv-clear-prefix, requeue-job, rotate-secret). The runner enforces a policy ACL and signs audit events before returning a success/failure envelope.
- The Console surface will provide a preview modal with resolved parameters and a dry-run log. Execution requires a two-step confirmation if the action is tagged 'destructive'.
- Shortcutlets can be composed into a flow (sequence or conditional DAG) to cover common incident scenarios. Each composed flow produces a single correlated audit trace and telemetry span for SLO analysis.
- Safety controls: dry-run-only mode, rate limiter (per-operator + global), approval gating for high-impact flows (need 2 approvals), and automatic fallback to a reversible safe-state if a step fails.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Keep surface area small for initial rollout: implement 6 core SDK actions and 4 example shortcutlets covering cache eviction, service restart, token rotation + rebalance, and incident triage scaffolding.
- Avoid building a Turing-complete orchestration engine; prefer simple sequence/conditional primitives. If needs grow, split orchestration into a follow-up epic.
- Security: require KMS signing for audit blobs and SSO-based operator identity. Must work with Dedicated and Private deployments (runner can be deployed in-customer for Private installs).

Telemetry & observability: each step emits structured events with correlation_id, operator, inputs (redacted), duration, success, and error codes. Add Console dashboard showing median time-to-execute and frequency of shortcutlet usage.

Deliverables:
- Shortcutlet manifest spec (Confluence) and validator CLI.
- Runner service with 6 helper actions and audit integration.
- Console modal + dry-run/preview UX.
- 4 composed production flows and docs for SRE/oncall.
acceptance_criteria: Operator can run an example 'cache-evict-and-restart' shortcutlet from the Console modal with a dry-run preview.
Execution produces a signed audit event persisted to audit-log (queryable via Console) with correlation_id.
All core helper actions include idempotency tokens and safe rollback instructions; automated rollback triggers on step failure.
Runner enforces ACLs and respects approval gating for high-impact flows; attempts without permission return clear error codes.
A GitHub PR (ops-tooling) with runner + manifest validator is merged and unit/integration tests cover success/failure/rollback paths.
Documentation (Confluence) and a 1-hour oncall walkthrough session scheduled; dashboard tile created in Datadog showing run frequency and median execution time.
